title: UK Landscape: Tees and Lake District

walkthroughs.body_html:
The River Tees rises in the high Pennines.

It flows about 137 km east to a wide estuary at Middlesbrough.

Its valley shows the full long profile.

Look out for High Force.

The Tees plunges 21 m over a hard whinstone sill onto soft limestone.

The waterfall slowly retreats, leaving a gorge.

The Lake District is a glaciated upland.

Scafell Pike reaches 978 m.

Tourism brings jobs but causes path erosion and traffic at honeypots like Tarn Hows.

mcqs.q: How does an oxbow lake form from a meander?
options: Oxbow lakes form where two rivers meet and one stops flowing.
Oxbow lakes form when meanders dry up completely.
Anticyclones bring heavy rainfall because they trap moisture.
Erosion on outside bends narrows the meander neck; during a flood the river cuts across the neck, deposition seals the old loop, leaving a horseshoe-shaped lake.

mcqs.q: What is lag time on a storm hydrograph?
options: Anticyclones bring heavy rainfall because they trap moisture.
Lag time is how long the storm itself lasts.
Lag time is the delay between thunder and lightning.
The time between peak rainfall and peak river discharge — affected by drainage basin shape, land use, soil saturation and vegetation.
